How databases connect related data

The previous lesson introduced several ways to organize data. Now compare how three databases connect related records. When you open an order, how does the shop know which product you bought and how many you ordered? Follow the same order through PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Neo4j.

One order in three databases

The four panels show three databases. MongoDB appears twice because an order can hold item details directly or point to a separate product document.

{
  "orderId": 101,
  "items": [
    { "productId": 1, "name": "Notebook", "quantity": 2 }
  ]
}

PostgreSQL · Follow the foreign keys

Start with the middle table, order_items. In this row, order_id points to order 101 and product_id points to product 1, the Notebook. These two columns are foreign keys. The quantity of 2 belongs to this order line. A JOIN matches the IDs so the shop can display the product name and quantity together.

SELECT products.name, order_items.quantity
FROM order_items
JOIN products ON products.id = order_items.product_id
WHERE order_items.order_id = 101;

MongoDB · Store details inside the order

PostgreSQL matched IDs across tables to get the name and quantity. With MongoDB, one option is to keep both values inside the order. In the upper-right panel, the order document contains an items list. One entry holds both the name Notebook and the quantity 2. This is embedding. Reading the order also retrieves those details. It works well for a receipt that should keep the item name as it was at checkout.

db.orders.findOne({ _id: 101 }, { items: 1 });

// Example result:
// { _id: 101, items: [{ name: "Notebook", quantity: 2 }] }

MongoDB · Link to a product by ID

In the lower-left panel, the order item stores product_id and quantity. To find the name, use product_id 1 to look up the product document whose _id is 1. This is referencing. Many orders can refer to the same product, so its current catalog details can be updated in one place.

const order = db.orders.findOne({ _id: 101 });
const item = order.items[0];
const product = db.products.findOne({ _id: item.product_id });
printjson({ name: product.name, quantity: item.quantity });

Neo4j · Connect the order and product directly

A MongoDB reference points to the product by ID. In a graph database the connection itself is stored as a relationship. In the lower-right panel, Order and Product are nodes. Follow the arrow from Order to Product. Its label, CONTAINS, tells you the product is part of the order. The quantity of 2 is stored on that relationship because it describes how many notebooks this particular order contains.

MATCH (:Order {id: 101})-[line:CONTAINS]->(product:Product)
RETURN product.name AS product, line.quantity AS quantity;
